title: Hold a lesson's load steady
statement: Count every moment that asks a learner to respond against a target budget for the lesson, and pair any addition that stays with a deletion.
example: One checklist sets about 31 answer moments per lesson as the target and records about 55 as a breach.
detail: The reading project's QC checklist counts discrete answer moments, clozes and your-turn beats included, rather than questions, with about 31 as what it calls the proven target and about 55 as the documented breach (`grade3-reading/artifacts/AlphaRead-QC-Checklist-v2-2026-09-04.md`, B15). A curriculum adherence audit of four lessons judged every page added beyond the design under a conservation rule, in which an addition that stays pairs with a deletion (`grade3-reading/artifacts/curriculum-adherence-2026-09-24/REPORT.md`), and its critic noted 11 added pages with no design basis in one lesson alone (`grade3-reading/artifacts/curriculum-adherence-2026-09-24/CRITIC.md`). Checks that interrupt every paragraph become compliance theater.
against: The budget is a count, not a measured time: in the audited lessons the 25-minute envelope was likely blown but unmeasured (`grade3-reading/artifacts/curriculum-adherence-2026-09-24/CRITIC.md`). The target itself was left open: "Ruled: document, don’t cut cosmetically; revisit when canonical videos land."
